hypothesis: Grouping parcels near the earliest-deadline anchor, within a limited deadline band, reduces route mixing and morning lateness.
selection_rule: Start with the earliest-deadline feasible parcel, breaking ties by current distance and ID. At each later step, find all feasible parcels; consider deadlines at most band minutes after the earliest feasible deadline; rank by distance from the first stop, current-leg distance, deadline, then ID.

fixed_components.waiting_rule: Same all-deliveries-at-least-ten-minutes-early check as the locked policy, before 2-opt

choose_candidate: Lowest total penalty on days 1-10 only; ties use smaller deadline band.
adoption_gate: Chosen candidate must not increase days 1-10 penalty and must improve days 11-20 penalty by at least 2%, with no hard-constraint or input-mutation violations.
limits: All 20 days have been used before. This is a split comparison on reused development data, not an unseen test. No additional settings will be added after seeing the results in this experiment.
checks: Geography can change selection only within the prescribed deadline band
Capacity, directed range and return cutoff
Duplicate, assigned and delivered parcel exclusion
Locked control replays match existing logs and metrics byte-for-byte
promotion: Do not modify main, the report or the submission ZIP. Present results for joint review.
